findings.title: Customer reports no friction with the platform
findings.description: When directly asked whether there was any friction on the platform, the customer said he hadn't hit any issues. He described his usage pattern as booking a session and showing up roughly twice a month, calling himself 'not a power user.' No defect or missing capability was identified.
findings.quote: Not that I've hit. I use it maybe twice a month, book a session, show up. It works.
findings.severity_reason: No defect reported; customer explicitly states the product works fine for his usage pattern.
findings.match_note: No catalogue match — this is an explicit absence-of-issue statement, not a defect or feature gap.

findings.title: Admin-side platform health inferred secondhand via office manager
findings.description: The customer stated that his office manager Cheryl handles the admin side of the account and that she would have told him loudly if anything were broken, taking her silence as evidence nothing is wrong. No specific admin-side defect was described firsthand by an external speaker.
findings.quote: My office manager, Cheryl, she's the one in the admin side. If something were broken, she'd have told me. Loudly.
findings.severity_reason: No concrete issue reported; this is secondhand reasoning about an absence of complaints, not a firsthand defect report.
findings.match_note: No catalogue match — no actual defect described, only inference from a third party's silence.

findings.title: Customer curious how coach-matching works, expresses satisfaction
findings.description: Customer asked how BetterBark pairs members with coaches (hand-matched vs. algorithmic) and was told it's a matching engine with human review for executive matches. He responded that the match worked well for him ('it nailed it'). No change or fix was requested.
findings.quote: How does that even work on your end? Do you hand-match or is it an algorithm?
findings.severity_reason: Purely informational question answered satisfactorily; no defect or feature gap raised.
findings.match_note: No catalogue match — customer is satisfied with matching outcome, no request for change.

findings.title: Coaching valued as a retention/recruiting tool, not a product complaint
findings.description: Customer explained the business value of the coaching benefit as a way to retain associates who might otherwise leave for higher pay, calling it the real ROI. This is commentary on program value/pricing justification, not a defect in or missing capability of the BetterBark product itself.
findings.quote: It helps me keep good associates from jumping to firms that offer more money. That's worth the check.
findings.severity_reason: Business-value commentary, not a product defect or feature request.
findings.match_note: No catalogue match — this is ROI/retention framing, not a product capability gap.
